Definition: Sitnah, the name of a well in Pal
BiblicalUsage: Sitnah was a well Isaac dug, and he named it for the strife that followed it. The herdsmen of Gerar strove for it as they had striven for Esek, so Isaac called it Sitnah, accusation, and moved on to dig again.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Isaac's wells teach me when to walk away. He did not fight for Sitnah; he dug another well, and I hold that peace is sometimes worth more than the water.
